evidence.claim: AccessControlHooks.onQueueWithdrawal lacks an isHooked check, so any caller can invoke it directly with an arbitrary lender and hooksData, reaching role providers' validateCredential with attacker-chosen data and consuming a lender's one-time credential, causing a delayed DoS of that lender's withdrawal/deposit.
evidence.support_reason: onQueueWithdrawal (812-825) has no `_hookedMarkets[msg.sender].isHooked` check (unlike onDeposit 775-776, onTransfer 858-860, and FixedTermLoanHooks.onQueueWithdrawal 855-856). With msg.sender = attacker, isKnownLenderOnMarket[lender][attacker] is false, so _tryValidateAccess (698) -> _tryValidateAccessInner (654) -> _handleHooksData (617) -> _tryValidateCredential (525) calls the attacker-selected provider with attacker-supplied data. The path is reachable by any EOA.
preconditions: A role provider whose validateCredential is stateful (consumes a one-time voucher) and whose TTL is shorter than the delay before the victim's transaction lands
Victim's transaction is delayed past the cached credential's TTL (the report's miner/censorship step)
